aliases: Museum of Fine Arts of the City of Paris

claims.text: The elegant Petit Palais was built by architect Charles Girault specifically to complement the Grand Palais for the 1900 universal exhibition.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It was actually constructed partly on the ruins of the older Palais de l'Industrie, which had been demolished just a few years prior in 1896.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The building is masterfully designed around a peaceful semi-circular garden courtyard.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The original exhibition spaces were brilliantly designed to be illuminated entirely by natural sunlight pouring through large windows and transparent domes.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Following the exhibition, it became the official Museum of Fine Arts for the City of Paris.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, it displays a vast permanent collection of historic artworks and artifacts spanning from ancient history up to around 1914.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The museum's holdings were massively enriched in 1902 when brothers Eugène and Auguste Dutuit generously donated their massive private collection of major artworks.
claims.subject: self
